name: Taiwan

facts.religion: Buddhist and Taoist folk religion about 70%, Christian about 5%

snapshot: An opposition-run legislature held up Taiwan's budget and weapons purchases for months under Chinese blockade drills, before Lai proposed a record defence budget.
culture: Taiwan's culture blends Hoklo, Hakka, mainland Chinese and Indigenous Austronesian heritage. Night markets, bubble tea and temple festivals like the Mazu pilgrimage draw huge crowds. Taiwan was the first place in Asia to legalise same-sex marriage, in 2019. A distinct Taiwanese identity has grown, especially among the young.
society: Taiwan makes most of the world's most advanced chips, led by TSMC, which has made it central to the global economy and to US-China rivalry. It went from martial law to full democracy in the 1990s. Beijing claims the island and stages large military drills around it. Conscription was extended to a year in 2024.
situation: Since 1949, when Chiang Kai-shek's defeated Nationalists fled to Taiwan, Beijing has claimed the island and vowed to take it, by force if necessary. Taiwan became a democracy in the 1990s, and most of its 23 million people now see themselves as Taiwanese, not Chinese. Its chip factories make most of the world's advanced semiconductors, which is why a war there would wreck the global economy.

The year began under threat: on 29 December 2025 China launched its "Justice Mission 2025" live-fire drills, simulating a blockade and port seizures (JURIST). President Lai Ching-te called 2026 "a crucial year" and pushed for a $40 billion special defence budget over eight years, including a "Taiwan Dome" air defence system. But the opposition Kuomintang and Taiwan People's Party, which control parliament and favour closer ties with Beijing, blocked it and held up the whole 2026 budget for months, the longest delay in nearly three decades, putting $2.4 billion in weapons and training at risk (Al-Monitor). The budget finally passed in August. Days later, Lai's cabinet proposed a record NT$1.12 trillion ($35 billion) defence budget for 2027, 3 percent of GDP, plus a NT$10,000 cash handout to every citizen from the AI chip boom that has sent the economy soaring (Bloomberg via The Edge). Local elections on 28 November will test both camps.
power: A semi-presidential democracy. The directly elected president, limited to two four-year terms, controls defence and foreign policy and appoints the premier; the 113-seat Legislative Yuan passes budgets and laws. Only 12 countries formally recognise Taiwan.
holders: President Lai Ching-te (DPP), since 2024; Premier Cho Jung-tai.
